long_biography.plain_text:
Before building a publishing business, Stuart W. Arnold worked in California and New York as an editor and boating journalist. After moving to St Petersburg in 1973, he devised a classified magazine that paired photographs with advertisements for cars. Auto Trader expanded through franchises and related titles covering classic cars, aircraft, boats and motorcycles.

Arnold sold the business to Cox Enterprises in 1988 and remained under a five-year management contract. He then turned a warehouse complex into CPN Television, investing in production technology and studio space for commercial, television and film work. The venture reflects the pattern of his career: he repeatedly applied publishing and media infrastructure to businesses assembled from scratch, first in print and later in screen production.
